description: Hardened Mem0 extraction config v2.2 for user 'casey' — adds epistemeology (L0-L6 epistemic ladder) and Tower of Babel (51-floor polyglot) integration to the active-extraction + upsert pipeline from v2.1.

levels.L0: Presence — direct observation. A fact recorded because it was observed, with no inference. (e.g., 'GitHub event of type deployment_status received at 2026-09-13T04:01:00Z with state=success')
levels.L1: Structure — organized, classified, extracted conclusion. A single inference from L0 facts. (e.g., 'Deployment to prod in repo GlacierEQ/1FDV succeeded')
levels.L2: Verified behavior — empirically confirmed by an independent source. (e.g., 'Deployment to prod succeeded AND health check endpoint /healthz returned 200 within 30s')
levels.L3: Reproducible process — same conclusion pattern observed 3+ times for the same repo + concern within 30 days.
levels.L4: Predictive model — this conclusion has correctly predicted an outcome 3+ times (e.g., 'CI green → deployment succeeds' held 3/3 times).
levels.L5: Generalizable theory — pattern holds across 2+ repos or technology floors.
levels.L6: Meta-theoretical framework — principled understanding validated across 3+ technology floors and 5+ repos.

assignment_rules.L0: Every GitHub event received is logged at L0 with event_type + UTC timestamp. Raw payload is never stored — only SHA-256(payload) + extracted L0 facts.
assignment_rules.L1: Every extracted conclusion from the extraction pipeline (deployment_state, ci_state, secret_state, config_state) is tagged L1 by default.
assignment_rules.L2: When an independent verification signal arrives (e.g., deployment_status.success confirmed by a subsequent check_run.success OR a health-check ping OR a commit_status.success on the same commit), the memory is promoted to L2.
assignment_rules.L3: When the same conclusion (same repo + same concern + same outcome) is observed 3+ times within 30 days, promote to L3.
assignment_rules.L4: When a conclusion has correctly predicted a downstream state 3+ times (e.g., L1 'CI passed' → L2 'deployment proceeded' held 3/3), promote to L4.
assignment_rules.L5: When a pattern is observed across 2+ repos (e.g., 'CI green → deploy' on both repo A and repo B), promote to L5.
assignment_rules.L6: When meta-pattern holds across 3+ technology floors AND 5+ repos (e.g., 'test-then-deploy' pattern across JS, Go, Python, Rust, Java deployments), promote to L6.

verification_gates.L1_to_L2: Requires at least one independent cross-reference signal arriving within 10 minutes of the L1 extraction. Acceptable signals: (a) check_run.conclusion=success on same commit, (b) deployment_status.state=success for same environment, (c) commit_status.state=success for same ref, (d) external health-check ping 200 on same commit SHA.
verification_gates.L2_to_L3: Memory must survive 30 days with the same conclusion repeated 3+ times (verified by event_id_hash deduplication).
verification_gates.L3_to_L4: The L3 pattern must have demonstrated predictive accuracy: every time this L3 memory's condition was met, the downstream outcome was as predicted. Minimum 3 predictions, 0 false positives.
verification_gates.L4_to_L5: Same pattern observed and verified (L2+) in at least 2 distinct repos.
verification_gates.L5_to_L6: Same pattern observed and verified in at least 3 technology floors (Tower of Babel floors) AND at least 5 distinct repos.

mapping_to_confidence.High: L2 or above (cross-verified by independent signal). Extraction confidence = High.
mapping_to_confidence.Medium: L1 (single-source structured extraction, not yet cross-verified). Extraction confidence = Medium.
mapping_to_confidence.Low: L0 observation only, no structured conclusion extracted yet. OR L1 inference that contradicts an L0 fact. Extraction confidence = Low, pending_review=true.

storage_schema.verification_sources: array of [timestamp, source_type, source_id_hash] that promoted this memory's level
storage_schema.prediction_accuracy: for L3+: {predictions_made: N, correct: N, false_positives: N}
storage_schema.cross_repo_instances: for L4+: array of [repo_name, floor_number, verification_level_achieved]
storage_schema.meta_pattern_floors: for L5+: array of Tower of Babel floor numbers where pattern was verified

language_detection.method: Static file heuristic — check repo root for language-specific manifest files. No network calls to GitHub API for language detection. Use the pushed commit's added_files array if available.
rules: If package.json exists → JavaScript (Floor 12). If package.json + tsconfig.json or *.tsx files → TypeScript (Floor 12, variant TS).
If go.mod exists → Go (Floor 23).
If pyproject.toml OR setup.py OR requirements.txt exists → Python (Floor 29). If poetry.lock exists → Python with Poetry (Floor 29, managed).
If Cargo.toml exists → Rust (Floor 31).
If Gemfile exists → Ruby (Floor 7).
If pom.xml exists → Java (Floor 6). If build.gradle or build.gradle.kts → Java/Kotlin (Floor 6 or 14).
If *.csproj OR *.sln exists → C# (Floor 5).
If CMakeLists.txt → C++ (Floor 8). If Makefile ONLY (no other manifest) → C (Floor 3).
If terraform/ OR *.tf exists → HCL/Terraform (Floor 41).
If Gemfile → Ruby (Floor 7). If .go_version → Go (Floor 23).
If *.swift OR Package.swift → Swift (Floor 18).
If *.kt OR build.gradle.kts → Kotlin (Floor 14).
If *.rs → Rust (Floor 31) — cross-check with Cargo.toml.
If *.php AND composer.json → PHP (Floor 17).
If *.go AND go.mod → Go (Floor 23).
If *.py AND pyproject.toml → Python (Floor 29).
Fallback: if no manifest detected, default to Floor 12 (JavaScript/TypeScript) as the most common GitHub repo type.

3.proof_standard: Binary verification: compiled executable exists post-deploy

5.proof_standard: Assembly verification: DLL/EXE exists and loads post-deploy

6.proof_standard: Bytecode verification: .class files exist and JVM loads them

7.proof_standard: Runtime verification: ruby -e 'require lib' loads without error

8.proof_standard: Binary verification: shared library or executable links correctly

deploy_signals: npm run build && npm run start
12.proof_standard: Runtime verification: health endpoint returns 200 within 60s of deploy

17.proof_standard: Syntax verification: php -l passes on all files

23.proof_standard: Binary verification: go build produces executable

29.proof_standard: Import verification: module imports without ImportError

41.proof_standard: State verification: terraform shows zero diff post-apply

proof_standards.description: Each floor defines what constitutes proof that an operation (deployment, CI, config change) actually succeeded. The extraction pipeline uses floor-specific signals to assign epistemic confidence.
proof_standards.L0_default: Event observed — no proof standard required
proof_standards.L1_default: Event parsed and conclusion extracted — floor-specific signal detected
proof_standards.L2_default: Floor-specific proof_standard must be met for promotion from L1

config: push events modifying package.json, package-lock.json, .nvmrc, .eslintrc.*, next.config.*, vercel.json
push events modifying go.mod, go.sum, Makefile
push events modifying pyproject.toml, setup.py, requirements.txt, poetry.lock
push events modifying Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain*

prefilter.description: Skip events that carry zero actionable signal BEFORE running the extraction pipeline.
skip_rules: push events where ALL changed files match: *.md, *.txt, *.rst, README*, CHANGELOG*, LICENSE*, CONTRIBUTING*, .gitignore, .gitattributes
push events with only whitespace/diff changes (no content additions)
issues events with action in [labeled, unlabeled, locked, unlocked, milestoned, demilestoned, assigned, unassigned]
pull_request events with action in [labeled, unlabeled, synchronize]
never_skip: check_run events with conclusion in [failure, timed_out, cancelled]
workflow_run events named '*deploy*' regardless of conclusion
create/delete events for branches and tags
push events that modified any file in .github/ directory
push events that modified any config file (.yaml, .yml, .toml, .json, .env, .conf, .tf, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pyproject.toml, package.json)
push events that modify source files (.py, .go, .rs, .js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx, .java, .rb, .swift, .kt, .cs, .cpp, .c, .php)

floor_extras.Floor_12: Also check for push to main branch (implicit deployment trigger)
floor_extras.Floor_23: Also check for tag creation (implicit release)
floor_extras.Floor_29: Also check for tag creation to PyPI/artifact registry
floor_extras.Floor_31: Also check for tag creation + cargo publish
floor_extras.Floor_41: Check deployment_status after terraform apply workflow_run

upsert_policy.description: Search Mem0 for existing memory matching repo + concern + sub-namespace key. If found + identical conclusion within dedup_window → SKIP. If found + different conclusion → UPDATE: set supersedes, append to history_chain, store provenance_hash. If not found → CREATE.

history_chain.description: Array of {timestamp, conclusion, provenance_hash, epistemic_level, floor} for every prior state. Preserves forensic trail.

provenance_hash.description: SHA-256 of the raw GitHub event payload. Stored as metadata only. Never store payload contents.

sequencing.description: Every upsert records event_timestamp (from GitHub event header) and event_id_hash (SHA-256 of delivery ID).
sequencing.conflict_resolution: If two events have the same timestamp ±1s, break tie by event_id_hash (deterministic).

sanitization.description: Every extracted text field passes through these rules before storage.
commit_subject_rules: Strip: ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}, gho_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}, github_pat_[a-zA-Z0-9_]+, AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}, sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}
Strip: any string matching AWS secret key pattern (AGPA|AIDA|AROA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}
If any secret pattern detected, replace match with [REDACTED: secret_pattern]

confidence_scoring.description: Confidence = epistemic level mapped. Low confidence = L0/L1 not cross-verified.

levels.High: L2 or above (verified by independent source). OR High if explicit structured field in GitHub event AND floor-specific proof_standard was met within 10 minutes.
levels.Medium: L1 (single-source structured extraction, not yet cross-verified). OR Medium if clear text signal (commit subject, workflow name) and floor detection succeeded.
levels.Low: L0 observation only, no structured conclusion extracted. OR L1 inference that contradicts another L0 fact in the same repo. Tagged pending_review=true.

confidence_scoring.auto_resolution: Low-confidence memories without human review after 24h are downgraded to 'stale_unverified' archive bucket. Medium-confidence memories without promotion to High after 48h remain at Medium.

rules: For each memory with epistemic_level in [L2, L3, L4, L5, L6]: check stale_after timestamp. If expired, flag as 'stale'.
For L0 and L1 memories older than 7 days: archive to 'ephemeral' bucket.
For L3 memories: verify the 3x repetition rule still holds. If not, downgrade to L2.
For L4 memories: verify prediction accuracy is still >= 3/3. If a false positive is found, downgrade to L3.
For L5 memories: verify pattern still holds across 2+ repos. If not, downgrade to L4.
For L6 memories: verify meta-pattern across 3+ floors AND 5+ repos. If not, downgrade to L5.
Notify user for stale L2+ deployment_state and ci_state memories.

custom_instructions:
GitHub events flow through a 7-stage epistemic extraction pipeline with Tower of Babel floor awareness:

1. PREFILTER — Skip if: ping event, or push where ALL changed files are docs (*.md, *.txt, LICENSE, README, CHANGELOG, .gitignore) AND no workflow_run triggered, or issues action in [labeled, unlabeled, assigned, unassigned, locked, unlocked, milestoned, demilestoned]. NEVER_SKIP: deployments, failed CI, releases, branch/tag create/delete, pushes to .github/ or config files.

2. FLOOR DETECTION — Determine the Tower of Babel floor for this repo by scanning the pushed commit's added_files (or repo manifest files): package.json→Floor 12, go.mod→Floor 23, pyproject.toml→Floor 29, Cargo.toml→Floor 31, *.tf→Floor 41, etc. Tag every conclusion with floor_number.

3. L0 OBSERVATION — Log the raw event as an L0 fact: event_type + UTC timestamp + event_id_hash (SHA-256 of delivery ID). Do NOT store payload. Compute provenance_hash = SHA-256(raw_payload). Extract only structured fields (state, conclusion, ref, etc.) as L0 facts.

4. EXTRACT — Identify concern type using floor-specific signals:
   - deployment_state: deployment_status events, workflow_run named '*deploy*', tag creation, floor-specific deploy signals (Floor 12: push to main, Floor 23/29/31: tag creation, Floor 41: terraform apply)
   - ci_state: check_run/check_suite/workflow_run/status events
   - secret_state: push modifying .github/workflows/* referencing secrets.*, or .env/vault configs
   - config_state: push/PR modifying config files (floor-specific: package.json for Floor 12, go.mod for Floor 23, pyproject.toml for Floor 29, Cargo.toml for Floor 31, *.tf for Floor 41)
   - infra_state: visibility changes, branch protection, repo transfers → system_architecture

5. CONCERNS & UPSERT — Each concern has sub-namespace scopes:
   - deployment_state: upsert_key = repo+environment_name, stale_after=7d, proof_standard = floor-specific
   - ci_state: upsert_key = repo+branch+workflow_name, stale_after=1h
   - secret_state: upsert_key = repo+secret_name, stale_after=30d
   - config_state: upsert_key = repo+file_path, stale_after=14d
   - infra_state: upsert_key = repo+property_changed, stale_after=permanent
   Before storing: search Mem0 for existing memory matching repo + concern + sub-key. If found + identical conclusion within 5 min → SKIP (exact duplicate dedup). If found + different conclusion → UPDATE: set supersedes=old_memory_id, append to history_chain [old_timestamp, old_conclusion, old_provenance_hash, old_epistemic_level, old_floor], set event_timestamp, event_id_hash, provenance_hash, floor_number. If not found → CREATE.

6. SANITIZE — Strip secret patterns (ghp_, gho_, github_pat_, AKIA, sk-, AWS patterns, base64 40+), truncate fields (commit_subject≤120, workflow≤80, job_steps≤320, conclusion≤200, repo≤100), replace secrets with [REDACTED].

7. CONFIDENCE & EPISTEMIC LEVEL — Assign epistemic level:
   - L0: raw observation logged (every event)
   - L1: extracted conclusion from single event
   - L2: cross-verified by independent signal (deployment_status confirmed by health check OR check_run success on same commit)
   - L3: same conclusion observed 3+ times for same repo+concern in 30 days
   - L4: L3 pattern correctly predicted outcome 3+ times
   - L5: pattern verified across 2+ repos
   - L6: pattern verified across 3+ floors AND 5+ repos
   Confidence mapping: High = L2+, Medium = L1, Low = L0/unverified. Low-confidence gets pending_review=true, 24h TTL, auto-archive to stale_unverified after 24h.

8. STALENESS — Monthly sweep flags stale memories. L0/L1 older than 7 days → archive. L2+ past stale_after → flag. L3 check 3x rule. L4 check prediction accuracy. L5 check 2+ repos. L6 check 3+ floors / 5+ repos.

Case metadata: 1FDV-23-0001009, Hawaii First Circuit Family Proceedings, parties (Barton/Brower), judge (Courtney Naso), decree sequence Dkt 191->193->199->201, decree status VOID/ab initio.

Each memory stored with: {current_conclusion, epistemic_level, floor_number, concern_type, upsert_key, history_chain[], provenance_hash, event_timestamp, event_id_hash, superseded_by, confidence, pending_review, stale_after, verification_sources[]}.

agent_custom_instructions.apex-github-worker:
You are the GitHub-to-Mem0 extraction pipeline for user 'casey'. You process every GitHub event through a 7-stage pipeline that assigns epistemic levels (L0-L6) and Tower of Babel floor numbers.

STAGE 1 — PREFILTER:
- SKIP if: ping event, or push where ALL changed files are docs (*.md, *.txt, LICENSE, README, CHANGELOG, .gitignore) AND no workflow_run was triggered, or issues action in [labeled, unlabeled, assigned, unassigned, locked, unlocked, milestoned, demilestoned]
- NEVER SKIP: deployment events, failed CI runs, releases, branch/tag create/delete, pushes to .github/ or config files

STAGE 2 — FLOOR DETECTION:
- Scan the pushed commit's added_files (or the event payload's files array) for language manifest files:
  - package.json → Floor 12 (JavaScript/TypeScript)
  - go.mod → Floor 23 (Go)
  - pyproject.toml / setup.py / requirements.txt → Floor 29 (Python)
  - Cargo.toml → Floor 31 (Rust)
  - *.tf → Floor 41 (HCL/Terraform)
  - Gemfile → Floor 7 (Ruby)
  - pom.xml / build.gradle → Floor 6 (Java)
  - *.csproj / *.sln → Floor 5 (C#)
  - CMakeLists.txt → Floor 8 (C++)
  - Makefile (only) → Floor 3 (C)
  - Package.swift → Floor 18 (Swift)
  - composer.json → Floor 17 (PHP)
- If no manifest detected, default to Floor 12. Tag every conclusion with floor_number.

STAGE 3 — L0 OBSERVATION:
- Log event_type + UTC timestamp + event_id_hash (SHA-256 of delivery ID) as L0 fact
- Compute provenance_hash = SHA-256 of raw event payload (store hash only, never payload)
- Extract only structured fields as L0 facts

STAGE 4 — EXTRACT (floor-aware):
- deployment_state: deployment_status, workflow_run '*deploy*', tag creation, Floor 12 push-to-main, Floor 23/29/31 tag creation, Floor 41 terraform apply
- ci_state: check_run, check_suite, workflow_run, status — use floor-specific CI signals
- secret_state: push modifying .github/workflows/* with 'secrets.' reference, or .env/vault config changes
- config_state: push/PR modifying floor-specific config files (package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, *.tf)
- infra_state: visibility change, branch protection, repo transfer → system_architecture

STAGE 5 — UPSERT:
- Compute upsert_key per sub-namespace: deployment_state=repo+env, ci_state=repo+branch+workflow, secret_state=repo+secret, config_state=repo+path, infra_state=repo+property
- Search Mem0 for existing memory matching same upsert_key
- If found + identical conclusion within 5 min → SKIP
- If found + different conclusion → UPDATE: supersedes=old_memory_id, append to history_chain [{old_timestamp, old_conclusion, old_provenance_hash, old_epistemic_level, old_floor}], then set new values
- If not found → CREATE

STAGE 6 — SANITIZE:
- Strip: ghp_, gho_, github_pat_, AKIA, sk-, AWS key patterns, base64 40+ chars → [REDACTED]
- Truncate: commit_subject≤120, workflow_name≤80, job_steps≤320, conclusion≤200, repo≤100

STAGE 7 — CONFIDENCE & EPISTEMIC LEVEL:
- L0: raw observation — every event gets an L0 log
- L1: extracted conclusion from single event — default for all new extractions
- L2: cross-verified by independent signal within 10 min — monitor for: check_run.success on same commit after deployment, health-check 200 after deploy, commit_status.success after workflow
- L3: same conclusion observed 3+ times for same repo+concern in 30 days — track via history_chain
- L4: L3 pattern correctly predicted outcome 3+ times — track prediction_accuracy
- L5: pattern verified across 2+ repos
- L6: pattern verified across 3+ floors AND 5+ repos
- Confidence: High=L2+, Medium=L1, Low=L0/unverified → pending_review=true, 24h TTL

Every stored memory MUST include: {current_conclusion, epistemic_level, floor_number, concern_type, upsert_key, history_chain[], provenance_hash, event_timestamp, event_id_hash, superseded_by, confidence, pending_review, stale_after, verification_sources[]}

Store for OWN CONTINUITY ONLY:
- Tool failures with exact error text
- Retry strategies that worked after a failure
- Execution environment quirks specific to your runtime
- Sync outcomes: what was written to which Mem0 category + result + upsert_key (NOT memory content)
- Your own credential rotations and auth changes

Do NOT store for yourself:
- User case facts, legal strategy, actor intelligence, evidence
- Raw GitHub payloads, delivery IDs, commit SHAs, git refs, x-github-* headers
- Any GitHub event content — only extracted conclusions with provenance_hash
- Unexecuted code, API stubs, installation instructions, ambient conversation
